title: Rust: Functions
description: Define and call functions with parameters and return values in Rust.

steps.title: Basic Function
steps.description: Define a function `greet` that prints `"Hi!"` and call it from `main`.
hints: Functions can be defined before or after main.

verification.failureMessage: Define and call a function that prints 'Hi!'.

steps.title: Function with Parameters
steps.description: Write a function `say_hello(name: &str)` that prints `"Hello, NAME!"` and call it with your name.

steps.title: Return Values
steps.description: Write a function `add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32` that returns the sum and print the result of `add(3, 7)`.
hints: `fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a + b }`
The last expression in a function is returned (no semicolon!).

verification.failureMessage: Write add(a, b) that returns a+b and print the result of 3+7.

steps.title: Function with Expression Body
steps.description: Write a function `square(x: i32) -> i32` that returns x*x using a single expression (no curly braces). Call and print `square(5)`.
hints: In Rust, the last expression is returned automatically.
Don't add a semicolon after `x * x` if you want it returned.

verification.failureMessage: Write square(x) that returns x*x and print square(5).

steps.title: Multiple Parameters and Early Return
steps.description: Write a function `max(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32` that returns the larger of two numbers using `if/else`. Print `max(8, 15)`.
hints: `if a > b { a } else { b }` — this is an expression!
The if/else expression returns a value.

verification.failureMessage: Write max(a, b) that returns the larger number.
